sessions.empty: No closed sessions in this workspace yet
sessions.resumeSkills.body: Adjust what "{{session}}" starts with before launching it. Neither skills nor the environment can be changed once the agent is running.
sessions.resumeSkills.missingHint: The session had these, but they aren't installed anymore. Install them from the Marketplace to use them here.
sessions.resumeSkills.unchanged: Same skills the session had when it was closed.
sessions.resumeSkills.diff: {{added}} added · {{removed}} removed, compared to what the session had.

sessions.filters.search: Search by title, agent or folder…
sessions.export.title: Export session
sessions.delete.confirm: Remove this session from the history? The agent's session file on your disk is left untouched.
sessions.missingSkills.title: This session is missing skills
sessions.missingSkills.body: "{{session}}" had skills that are no longer installed ({{count}}). If you open it as is, the agent won't have them.
sessions.missingSkills.allRestored: All the skills "{{session}}" had are back. You can open it.
sessions.missingSkills.substituted: The original copy is gone; another installed one with the same name is used
sessions.missingSkills.ambiguous: The original copy is gone and several share that name — pick which one to install
sessions.missingSkills.notFound: Missing — not in any added repository

terminal.empty: Open a project from Home to get started
wizard.step3.helper: These get attached before the agent starts, so they're already available from the first message.
wizard.step3.empty: You haven't installed any skill yet — you can continue without picking any.
wizard.step3.noneCompatible: No installed skill declares compatibility with this agent — you can continue without picking any.
settings.terminal.desc: How terminal history looks and how you move through it.
settings.terminal.marks.desc: Draws a faint line every time you send something, so one turn is visibly separated from the next when scrolling back through a long conversation.
settings.terminal.marks.limits: It keys off the Enter key, which is all the terminal can see: an Enter inside a multi-line message marks too. It does not apply to full-screen TUIs (OpenCode), where there is no scrollback to anchor the mark to.
settings.terminal.marks.applies: Applies to terminals you open from now on; already-open ones are unchanged.
settings.title: Settings
settings.appearance.desc: Switch between light and dark theme
settings.tuis.desc: Add tools not detected automatically (e.g. aider, continue, opencode)
settings.tuis.name: Name
settings.tuis.advancedDesc: None of this is required. Each field you fill in unlocks one more feature: resuming sessions, managing its skills, or showing its history.
settings.tuis.resumeArgsHint: Appended to the command to resume a session. Must include {session}. e.g. --resume {session} or resume {session}. Empty = this TUI always starts fresh.
settings.tuis.skillsDirHint: Relative to the project — where skill symlinks are created. e.g. .agents/skills or .mytui/skills. Empty = the app won't manage its skills.
settings.tuis.sessionsDirHint: Where this TUI stores its sessions. Accepts ~. e.g. ~/.mytui/sessions
settings.tuis.sessionIdFromHint: How to read the id from the session file
settings.orchestrator.desc: When an external agent drives the app through the CLI, every tab it watches sends it events and spends its context. This cap is what keeps it from filling up.
settings.orchestrator.watchLimitHint: Most tabs an orchestrator can follow with «ccode watch add» simultaneously.
settings.orchestrator.watchLimitWarning: Past 5 watched tabs, the events alone can fill the model's context before it finishes the task.
settings.skillsDir.desc: Where installed skills are stored globally. Changing it only affects future installs.
accounts.pickHint: The account is fixed now: the TUI reads it at startup, so it can't be changed later. For another account, open another agent.
terminal.accountMissing: This tab's account could not be used ({{error}}). Nothing was launched, to avoid starting with the wrong account.
settings.accounts.pendingLogin: This account still needs a sign-in
settings.accounts.emptyForAgent: You haven't added any account for this TUI yet.
settings.accounts.systemDefault: Your usual account is still there and is used whenever you don't pick one.
settings.accounts.noneInstalled: No installed TUI supports multiple accounts.
settings.accounts.unsupportedNote: Only TUIs that can move their login to another folder are listed. Gemini CLI and Kimi Code expose no way to do that, so giving them multiple accounts would end up with accounts overwriting each other.
settings.accounts.add.title: Add account
settings.accounts.add.name: Account name
settings.accounts.add.nameHelper: This is the folder name {{envVar}} points to. Letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.'
settings.accounts.add.taken: An account with that name already exists for this TUI.
settings.accounts.add.noneInstalled: No installed TUI supports multiple accounts.
settings.accounts.login.title: Sign in to "{{name}}"
settings.accounts.login.helper: This terminal runs "{{command}}" pointed at this account only. Sign in as usual; the app never sees your credentials. Closing it ends the process.
settings.accounts.delete.title: Remove "{{name}}"
settings.accounts.delete.body: You can remove it from the app and keep its files, or also delete the folder holding its login:
settings.cli.desc: Install the ccode command to drive the app from your terminal (or from another agent). No administrator permissions needed.
settings.cli.notInPath: That folder isn't in your PATH. If typing ccode in a terminal says the command isn't found, add this line to your shell profile:
settings.cli.copyNote: On Windows the executable is copied, so reinstall the CLI after updating the app.
settings.cli.noBinary: No ccode binary found next to the app. If you're running in development, build it with: cargo build --bin ccode
settings.cli.usage: Try it with: ccode app status · ccode --help
skills.install.title: Install skill from folder
skills.install.helper: Pick a local SKILL.md file to install
skills.install.metadataHelper: This skill is missing some metadata used for filtering later on. Filling it in is entirely optional — you can install as-is and add it anytime from the skill's editor.
skills.install.field.author: Author
skills.searchEmpty: No installed skill matches your search
skills.detail.title: Edit skill
skills.delete.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
skills.delete.bodyNone: This skill isn't attached to any project. Deleting it removes the global copy.
skills.delete.bodyImpact: This skill is currently attached to:
skills.attach.title: Attach "{{name}}"
skills.health.title: Broken skill symlinks
marketplace.registries.empty: You haven't added any repository yet
marketplace.registries.removeConfirm: Remove "{{name}}" from your repositories? Skills you already installed are not affected.
marketplace.registries.removeNoSkills: You haven't installed any skill from this repository, so nothing else is removed.
marketplace.registries.removeSkillsTitle: {{count}} installed skill(s) will also be deleted
marketplace.registries.removeSkillsHint: Their global copies are deleted and their symlinks are removed from every project using them. This cannot be undone.
marketplace.registries.deleteHint: Removing a repository also deletes the skills you installed from it — you'll see the full list before confirming.
marketplace.empty: No skills to show. Add a repository and refresh it, or try a different search.
marketplace.add.title: Add skills repository
marketplace.add.skillsShHelper: Leave empty to search the whole directory. Requires Node.js: it uses the official CLI (npx skills), not their API.
marketplace.add.name: Name
marketplace.add.githubHelper: Paste the repo link (https://github.com/owner/repo) or type it as owner/repo. Also owner/repo@branch and owner/repo:subfolder. Public repos only.
marketplace.add.error.required: Fill in the name and location
settings.prelaunch.desc: Commands that run before an agent starts, to put it in the right environment.
settings.prelaunch.hint: These are just saved here. Which ones to use, and in what order, is chosen per tab under Advanced options.
prelaunch.missingPreset: This saved command no longer exists
prelaunch.chainDesc: They run in order before the agent. If one fails, the agent won't start.
terminal.prelaunchError: Couldn't prepare this tab's environment ({{error}}). Nothing was launched, to avoid starting in the wrong environment.
sessions.resumeOptions.title: This session's options
terminal.skillSetupFailed: A skill could not be mounted: {{error}}
sessions.skillNoLongerInstalled: Skill '{{name}}' is no longer installed; the session reopened without it.
marketplace.registries.skillsShNotListab: Its catalogue can't be listed: it only answers searches, so refreshing never raises the count. The number is the last search's, not its size.
marketplace.skillsShNeedsQuery: skills.sh is searched along with your repositories, but its catalogue can't be listed: until you type something it shows 0 no matter how often you refresh.
skills.builder.title: Create your own skill
skills.builder.subtitle: Saved as a local skill: it is yours and no update overwrites it.
skills.builder.name: Name
skills.builder.nameHelper: This is how the agent will refer to it. Lowercase with dashes works best.
skills.builder.descriptionPlaceholder: What it does and when to use it
skills.builder.descriptionHelper: This is what the agent reads to decide whether to use it. Worth writing well.
skills.builder.agentsHelper: With none selected, the skill applies to all of them.
skills.builder.bodyPlaceholder:
# How to work on this project

Write here what the agent needs to know.
skills.detail.name: Name
skills.detail.fromRegistryNote: This skill came from {{registry}}. Saving creates your own copy and leaves the original untouched, still receiving repository updates.
skills.builder.bodyHint: What the agent reads when it uses this skill
settings.shortcuts.desc: Move around without leaving the keyboard. A section's shortcut also takes you back to the terminal when you're already there.
settings.shortcuts.terminalNote: These are handled before the terminal, so inside an agent they stop working as editing keys: Ctrl+M was Enter, Ctrl+H was Backspace, and Ctrl+E and Ctrl+K moved the cursor. Enter and Backspace have their own keys and still work.
workspaces.empty: No agents open yet. Open one and its folder shows up here.
explorer.noTab: With no agent open there is no folder to show.
settings.terminal.gpu.desc: Crisper text and smoother scrolling. It depends on your graphics driver: if you see flicker or blank terminals, turn it off and it falls back to normal drawing.
marketplace.preview.none: Pick a skill to read it before installing.
marketplace.preview.unavailable: This repository can't serve the skill without installing it, so only the listing data is shown.
accounts.usage.unsupported: This TUI does not record usage on disk, so there is nothing real to show.
accounts.usage.none: No activity in the last seven days.
accounts.usage.windowClosed: No window is open: this account hasn't been used in over 5 h.
accounts.usage.resetFromServer: Reset time reported by the server.
accounts.usage.resetDerived: Derived from the window's first message.
accounts.usage.noQuota: Token counts come from the TUI's own transcripts, so they're exact. How much the plan allows is NOT in any local file — Claude Code asks the API and doesn't store it — so there's no percentage to show without making it up.
accounts.plan.asking: Asking the TUI for your quota…
skills.palette.empty: No installed skill matches. Type to search the repositories.
skills.palette.pick: Pick a skill to read it before attaching.
skills.palette.note: Attaching writes one symlink inside {{dir}} and removes it when you detach. Nothing else on disk is touched.
skills.palette.noteTab: Attaching writes one symlink into that tab's skills folder and removes it when the tab closes. Nothing else on disk is touched.
skills.palette.searchHint: Type to search the repositories too.
newAgent.title: Open another agent here
skills.preview.none: Pick a skill to see its detail.
fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.card.openPaneHint: Pick this same session up in a terminal
fleet.empty.title: No agents in the background
fleet.empty.desc: Hand an agent a task and keep working — this is where you see what it is doing and what it needs from you.
fleet.new.title: Hand over a task
fleet.new.promptPlaceholder: Fix the failing test in containment.rs and run cargo test
fleet.new.name: Name
fleet.error.noWorkspace: Open a folder before launching an agent.
fleet.rules.title: Permission rules
fleet.rules.desc: What agents may do without asking you, or are never allowed to do, in
fleet.rules.empty: No rules yet: agents ask you about everything.
fleet.rules.syntax: Tool or Tool(pattern), with * as a wildcard: Read · Bash(git status*) · Edit(src/**). The first match wins.
fleet.card.takeOverHint: Stops the background agent and continues the same conversation in a terminal
fleet.new.isolateHint: A copy of the repo on a new branch, so it doesn't collide with other agents. Starts from the last commit: uncommitted work isn't there.
fleet.new.isolateNoRepo: Only for folders that are a git repository with at least one commit.
fleet.new.collision: {{n}} agent(s) are already working in this folder. Without a worktree they will edit the same files at once.
fleet.card.discardHint: Deletes the working copy. Refuses if there are uncommitted changes, and keeps the branch if it has its own commits.
fleet.worktree.discarded: Worktree discarded. Branch {{branch}} had nothing new and was deleted too.
fleet.worktree.discardedKept: Worktree discarded. Branch {{branch}} was kept: it has commits that exist nowhere else.
settings.rendering.gpu.desc: Off keeps text sharp: when WebKitGTK composites the window on the GPU, glyphs come out blurry. Turn it on only if the app feels slow on this machine.
settings.rendering.restart: Takes effect after restarting the app.
settings.rendering.env: The WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE variable in your environment overrides this option.
settings.terminal.gpu.noCompositing: Unavailable: without GPU compositing (Appearance) there is no WebGL, so the terminal is drawn with the DOM.
